# dtrexc

> Reorders the real Schur factorization of a real matrix A = Q·T·Qᵀ, so that the diagonal block of T with row index IFST is moved to row ILST.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtrexc from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtrexc';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtrexc( order, compq, N, T, LDT, Q, LDQ, ifst, ilst, WORK ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `compq` | `"none" \| "update"` | `'update'`: update the matrix Q of Schur vectors; `'none'`: do not update Q. |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix T.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, the upper quasi-triangular matrix T, in Schur Schur canonical form. On exit, the reordered upper quasi-triangular matrix, again in Schur canonical form. |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T`<br>Requires `LDT ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, if `compq === 'update'`, the matrix Q of Schur vectors. On exit, if `compq === 'update'`, Q has been postmultiplied by the orthogonal transformation matrix Z which reorders T. |
| ↳ `LDQ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Q`<br>Rejects `ldq < 1 \|\| (compq === 'update' && ldq < max(1, N))` |
| `ifst` | `Int32Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): ifst<br>Rejects `(ifst < 1 \|\| ifst > N) && N > 0` |
| `ilst` | `Int32Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): ilst<br>Rejects `(ilst < 1 \|\| ilst > N) && N > 0` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `N` elements |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `compq`:

  -   `= 'V'`: update the matrix Q of Schur vectors;
  -   `= 'N'`: do not update Q.
- `N`: The order of the matrix T. $N \ge 0$. If N == 0 arguments `ILST` and `IFST` may be any value.
- `T`: On entry, the upper quasi-triangular matrix T, in Schur Schur canonical form. On exit, the reordered upper quasi-triangular matrix, again in Schur canonical form.
- `Q`: On entry, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the matrix Q of Schur vectors. On exit, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, Q has been postmultiplied by the orthogonal transformation matrix Z which reorders T. If `COMPQ = 'N'`, Q is not referenced.
- `ilst`: Specify the reordering of the diagonal blocks of T. The block with row index `IFST` is moved to row `ILST`, by a sequence of transpositions between adjacent blocks. On exit, if `IFST` pointed on entry to the second row of a 2-by-2 block, it is changed to point to the first row; `ILST` always points to the first row of the block in its final position (which may differ from its input value by +1 or -1). $1 \le \mathrm{IFST} \le N$; $1 \le \mathrm{ILST} \le N$.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "none", "update"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` seventh argument is invalid (rejected when `LDQ < 1 \|\| ( compq === "update" && LDQ < max( 1, N ) )`)
- `RangeError` eighth argument is invalid (rejected when `( ifst[ 0 ] < 1 \|\| ifst[ 0 ] > N ) && N > 0`)
- `RangeError` ninth argument is invalid (rejected when `( ilst[ 0 ] < 1 \|\| ilst[ 0 ] > N ) && N > 0`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtrexc.ndarray(
    compq,
    N,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    Q, strideQ1, strideQ2, offsetQ,
    ifst,
    ilst,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Reorders the real Schur factorization of a real matrix A = Q_T_Q^T, so that.
the diagonal block of T with row index IFST is moved to row ILST.

The real Schur form T is reordered by an orthogonal similarity transformation
Z^T _ T _ Z, and optionally the matrix Q of Schur vectors is updated by
postmultiplication with Z.

T must be in Schur canonical form (as output by DHSEQR), that is, block
upper triangular with 1-by-1 and 2-by-2 diagonal blocks; each 2-by-2
diagonal block has its diagonal elements equal and its off-diagonal elements
of opposite sign.

Note: IFST and ILST are 1-based (Fortran convention). They may be adjusted
on return when they point to the second row of a 2-by-2 block.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `compq` | `"none" \| "update"` | `'update'` to update Q, `'none'` to not update Q |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix T<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · The upper quasi-triangular matrix |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of T |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of T |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for T |
| `Q` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Orthogonal matrix (updated if compq=`'update'`) |
| ↳ `strideQ1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of Q |
| ↳ `strideQ2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of Q |
| ↳ `offsetQ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for Q |
| `ifst` | `Int32Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): row index of the block to move (1-based)<br>Rejects `(ifst < 1 \|\| ifst > N) && N > 0` |
| `ilst` | `Int32Array` | **in/out** · Input/output (length-1 array): target row index (1-based)<br>Rejects `(ilst < 1 \|\| ilst > N) && N > 0` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length N |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `compq`:

  -   `= 'V'`: update the matrix Q of Schur vectors;
  -   `= 'N'`: do not update Q.
- `N`: The order of the matrix T. $N \ge 0$. If N == 0 arguments `ILST` and `IFST` may be any value.
- `T`: On entry, the upper quasi-triangular matrix T, in Schur Schur canonical form. On exit, the reordered upper quasi-triangular matrix, again in Schur canonical form.
- `Q`: On entry, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, the matrix Q of Schur vectors. On exit, if `COMPQ = 'V'`, Q has been postmultiplied by the orthogonal transformation matrix Z which reorders T. If `COMPQ = 'N'`, Q is not referenced.
- `ilst`: Specify the reordering of the diagonal blocks of T. The block with row index `IFST` is moved to row `ILST`, by a sequence of transpositions between adjacent blocks. On exit, if `IFST` pointed on entry to the second row of a 2-by-2 block, it is changed to point to the first row; `ILST` always points to the first row of the block in its final position (which may differ from its input value by +1 or -1). $1 \le \mathrm{IFST} \le N$; $1 \le \mathrm{ILST} \le N$.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "none", "update"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eleventh argument is invalid (rejected when `( ifst[ 0 ] < 1 \|\| ifst[ 0 ] > N ) && N > 0`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (rejected when `( ilst[ 0 ] < 1 \|\| ilst[ 0 ] > N ) && N > 0`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 1`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `= 1`: two adjacent blocks were too close to swap (the problem is very ill-conditioned); T may have been partially reordered, and `ILST` points to the first row of the current position of the block being moved.

</section>

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dtrexc from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtrexc';

const ifst = new Int32Array( 1 );
const ilst = new Int32Array( 1 );

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const T = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const Q = discreteUniform( N * N, -10, 10, opts );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
ifst[ 0 ] = 1;
ilst[ 0 ] = 1;
let out = {
	'info': dtrexc( 'column-major', 'update', N, T, N, Q, N, ifst, ilst, WORK ),
	'ifst': ifst[ 0 ],
	'ilst': ilst[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
ifst[ 0 ] = 1;
ilst[ 0 ] = 1;
out = {
	'info': dtrexc.ndarray( 'update', N, T, N, 1, 0, Q, N, 1, 0, ifst, ilst, WORK, 1, 0 ),
	'ifst': ifst[ 0 ],
	'ilst': ilst[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DTREXC`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTREXC reorders the real Schur factorization of a real matrix $A = Q \, T \, Q^T$, so that the diagonal block of T with row index `IFST` is moved to row `ILST`.

The real Schur form T is reordered by an orthogonal similarity transformation $Z^T \, T \, Z$, and optionally the matrix Q of Schur vectors is updated by postmultiplying it with Z.

T must be in Schur canonical form (as returned by DHSEQR), that is, block upper triangular with 1-by-1 and 2-by-2 diagonal blocks; each 2-by-2 diagonal block has its diagonal elements equal and its off-diagonal elements of opposite sign.

</section>
